plan_a_advantages: Dedicated threshold training sessions for speed development.
Two longer runs, providing ample time for aerobic base building and trail-specific endurance.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster, primarily because it incorporates dedicated threshold work alongside longer runs, directly addressing the goal of improving speed. While Plan B includes hill repeats, it lacks a focused approach to building the sustainable strength needed for faster trail running. Plan A’s structured tempo sessions are crucial for developing the physiological adaptations required for faster pace, whereas Plan B’s emphasis on recovery and easy runs might not sufficiently challenge the athlete to improve their speed. Furthermore, the repetition of threshold work in Plan A, combined with the longer runs, provides a more targeted approach to building the necessary aerobic and muscular endurance for trail racing.
